citations.quoted_value: Recursive discovery uses the same initialization-time captured ignore-path configuration as normal module expansion.
Add an end-to-end regression test that loads `ignore-paths = ["^src/gen/.*$"]` from project configuration and runs recursive linting on `src/`.
The repository does not establish whether recursive discovery is intended to use the live self.config.ignore_paths value or the captured self._ignore_paths value.

findings.description: The contract requires recursive discovery to use the initialization-time captured ignore-path configuration, but none of the acceptance checks mutates or otherwise differentiates the live configuration from the captured configuration. An implementation that continues using `self.config.ignore_paths` could satisfy the listed end-to-end checks, leaving a confirmed material decision unverified.
findings.general_cause: A material internal-state decision is stated without an acceptance check that distinguishes it from the alternative behavior.
findings.observable_signal: The regression scenario loads configuration normally, where the live and initialization-time captured ignore-path values can be identical; therefore it cannot prove recursive discovery actually uses the captured value.

citations.quoted_value: Add an end-to-end regression test that loads `ignore-paths = ["^src/gen/.*$"]` from project configuration and runs recursive linting on `src/`.

At base commit 3c5eca2ded3dd2b59ebaf23eb289453b5d2930f0, recursive discovery consults the live config.ignore_paths value while later module expansion uses the separately captured _ignore_paths value. Existing recursive-ignore tests cover command-line patterns containing leading wildcards, but not an anchored relative ignore-path loaded from project configuration.

findings.description: The regression check does not require `pyproject.toml` or the reported `[tool.pylint.MASTER]` configuration path. Because the requested failure specifically concerns an anchored ignore path supplied through project TOML, the contract can be accepted without reproducing that material input route.
findings.general_cause: The acceptance criteria generalize the reported configuration source and omit the specific configuration-loading path implicated by the request.
findings.observable_signal: The contract asks only for configuration loaded from an unspecified “project configuration,” so a test using another supported configuration format could pass without exercising TOML loading.

citations.quoted_value: Run and preserve all existing recursive-ignore tests.
Verify `ignore`, `ignore-patterns`, configuration precedence, and non-recursive behavior remain unchanged.
Existing end-to-end recursive ignore-path tests pass ignore paths on the command line as patterns beginning with '.*' and assert that the targeted failing file is absent from the linted paths.

findings.description: The contract declares preservation of `ignore`, `ignore-patterns`, configuration precedence, and non-recursive behavior, but provides no executable checks for those distinct guarantees. Running existing recursive-ignore tests only partially covers the first two and does not establish configuration precedence or non-recursive compatibility.
findings.general_cause: A broad compatibility requirement lacks concrete observable cases or a defined verification method.
findings.observable_signal: The final acceptance check groups four distinct behavior surfaces under “remain unchanged” without specifying representative inputs, expected outputs, or tests.

summary: The contract is not materially implementation-ready: it cannot verify the captured-versus-live configuration decision, does not require reproduction through the reported pyproject.toml configuration path, and states broad compatibility guarantees without executable acceptance criteria.
